entities.summary:
Scribonius Largus was the court physician to the Roman emperor Claudius, a position he held from approximately 47 CE until Claudius' assassination in 54 CE. As a renowned physician of his time, Scribonius Largus developed innovative treatments for various ailments and created a range of medicinal concoctions.

Largus' most notable creation was the famous 'posca,' a vinegar-based drink that became a staple among Roman soldiers. His work in the field of medicine contributed significantly to the development of Roman pharmacology, laying the groundwork for future advancements in medical science.

Scribonius Largus' legacy extends beyond his medical contributions. He played a pivotal role in shaping the imperial court's medical practices and was instrumental in promoting the use of herbal remedies among Roman rulers.

His influence on the Roman Empire's medical landscape can be seen in the numerous references to 'posca' found in ancient texts, including those of the Greek physician Galen. This enduring legacy is a testament to Scribonius Largus' lasting impact on the world of medicine and his place in the annals of history.

Scribonius Largus was a key figure in the Roman imperial court during a time of great change and upheaval. His work as a physician, particularly his development of 'posca,' had far-reaching consequences that continue to be felt today.
